fixes.explanation: Not quite, baker. God says the priesthood belongs to Aaron and his sons “by a permanent statute,” and that reaches well past one lifetime (Exodus 29:9). He also says Aaron's holy garments will pass to his sons after him (Exodus 29:29). Nobody sets up a hand-me-down plan for a job that ends with the first person wearing it.

Yes, waved, baker! God says the fat, thigh, loaf, cake and wafer go into the hands of Aaron and his sons, and they “…wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.” (Exodus 29:24) Hands full, arms moving, all of it done before the LORD. I get tired just carrying one full tray of cookies across my bakery, so I'm impressed.

That's the one, baker. Aaron's holy garments go to his sons after him, and God says the reason is so they can be anointed and ordained in them (Exodus 29:29). Same clothes, next set of priests. I'd hand my apron down too, but by now it's mostly flour.
